comments.author: @HoàngDuyMạnh-y8e
comments.text: I'm 47 and have lived in Alofi my entire life. Watching outsiders call us "forgotten" makes me laugh—we're just 1,600 people living quietly on a giant coral rock! People ask how we live without sandy beaches, but we just walk down the sea tracks to swim at Matapa Chasm or Limu Pools. The toughest part is waiting for the monthly cargo ship for fresh supplies, but the peace here is unbeatable. Drop your questions below if you want to know what daily life on the Rock is really like! 🇳🇺

replies.author: @TravelBeyond4K

comments.author: @Beyondhorizon-n6t
comments.text: The arrangement with New Zealand is a fascinating double-edged sword. It provides the essential infrastructure to keep the island functioning, yet that same citizenship makes it far too easy for the younger generation to leave. The 1,700 who choose to stay behind aren't just residents; they are the sole guardians of an entire culture.

comments.text: Local from Alofi here! Seeing our jagged limestone rock in 4K is wild.
